sentences.text: Shri Manish Saxena, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Shiraz Qureshi, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.
Heard on admission as well as on the question of maintainability.

This criminal revision is listed today for orders on the question of maintainability and for consideration of I.A. No.8240/2018, an application under Section 397 (1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of custodial sentence of applicant.

According to office note, it appears that on 14.09.2018 when criminal revision was filed, it was not clear from the criminal revision and annexed document that on that day applicant Vimal Chand Jain was in custody or not, as it is apparent from the judgment dated 08.08.2018 passed by lower appellate Court in criminal appeal No.245/2017 that on the date of passing of judgment by the Twelfth Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior, present applicant Vimal Chand Jain was absent before lower appellate Court.
On this point on behalf of applicant, certified copy of order sheets of JMFC, Gwalior dated 09.08.2018, 07.09.2018 & 22.10.2018 have been submitted, according to which present applicant Vimal Chand Jain appeared before the trial Court on 22.10.2018 and after verification regarding his identity on the basis of Adhar Card, he was taken into custody and sent to the Central Jail Gwalior for suffering the sentence awarded by the lower appellate Court and on same day, on prayer of applicant, trial Court also permitted present applicant to sign vakalatnama which was to be presented before this Court.

An affidavit THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Vimal Chand Jain Vs. State of M.P.) dated 30.10.2018 has also been filed by Vivek Jain son of present applicant regarding surrender of present applicant, therefore, it is clear that present applicant surrendered before trial Court on 22.10.2018 and since then he is in custody.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Vimal Chand Jain Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In these facts and circumstances, the criminal revision appears to be maintainable.
Criminal revision is admitted for final hearing.

Appearing counsel for the parties heard on I.A. No.
8240/2018, filed under Section 397(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of custodial sentence of the applicant.

sentences.text: No fresh notice is required to be sent to respondent/State as Shri Shiraz Qureshi learned counsel has already appeared on behalf of the respondent/State.

The applicant was convicted by the trial Court under Section 7 (1), 7 (2), 7 (3), 7 (5) [Rule 44 (J)] of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I with fine of Rs. 1000/-, six months R.I with fine of Rs.1000/-, till rising of the Court with fine of Rs. 500/- and six months R.I with fine of Rs. 1000/- respectively and sentence has been affirmed by the lower appellate Court.
Appearing counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant was released on bail during trial and previously his custodial sentence was suspended by the lower appellate Court and there is no possibility of early hearing of this criminal revision.

It is also contended by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is about 77 years old and he is suffering from several diseases, hence, it is prayed that custodial sentence of applicant be suspended during the pendency of this criminal revision, which is strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent/State.
THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Vimal Chand Jain Vs. State of M.P.)

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Vimal Chand Jain Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Considering the rival contentions of the parties, without commenting on the merits of the case, as there is no possibility of early hearing of this criminal revision before this Court, I.A. No.8240/2018 is allowed and it is ordered that on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 60,000/- (Rupees Sixty Thousand) by the applicant with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court for his regular appearance before the Registry of this Court firstly on 25.02.2019 and on such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry for the same purpose in future, the applicant's jail sentence be suspended and he be released on bail.

(Ashok Kumar Joshi) Judge Aman AMAN TIWARI 2018.11.01 15:32:47 +05'30'
